sampling_model.design: One consecutive trajectory in the fixed common path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) from a stationary regime \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\); identification is population-level and sampling uncertainty comes from temporal dependence.
sampling_model.units: Overlapping finite cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a)\) on the fixed product alphabet, indexed by their terminal time.
sampling_model.treatment: A hypothetical intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x)\); no experimental assignments are observed.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cylinder assignment in the fixed product alphabet has positive probability, hence every denominator cylinder used by the returned expression is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Probabilities of the returned \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders are estimated by empirical frequencies and their long-run covariance by the modified-Bartlett Newey--West estimator with \(h_T\to\infty\) and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives sufficient summary-graph front-door conditions and a common do-free expression for selected micro total effects under latent confounding.
The ID algorithm returns an observational functional or a hedge and is complete for a fixed finite ADMG.
Theorem 1.1 bounds the graph segment needed to decide identification for one fully specified periodic latent-confounded time-series graph.
A possible-c-component and region recursion is sound and complete for causal identification over the finite graph class represented by a PAG.
Fixing kernels and intrinsic sets characterize identifiable effects and nested constraints in a fixed ADMG.
Do-calculus is sound and complete for macro total effects in latent-confounded summary causal graphs.
A complete graphical characterization and two finite adjustment sets identify linear direct effects from summary causal graphs under no hidden confounding.
Under causal sufficiency, Theorem 2 gives sufficient summary-graph conditions and a finite adjustment set for singleton lag-specific total effects.
Necessary and sufficient conditions and a pseudo-linear algorithm characterize identification by common adjustment in causally sufficient summary graphs.
Graphical fixing outputs can be compiled into weight-based and influence-function estimators under independent sampling.

body.tldr: The full sound-and-complete lag-robust fixing theorem remains open, but the terminating three-way certified procedure now has a broader sound success region. In addition to the concrete outside-front-door witness and successful saturated ordinary-ID calls for acyclic loop-free directed summaries, it imports Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui's 2024 causally sufficient SCG criterion: when \(H\) has no bidirected edge, the procedure returns the marginal for the no-ancestor case or their explicit finite adjustment functional when neither listed cyclic or back-door obstruction holds. This branch covers eligible cyclic and self-looped summaries and is established by an explicit inclusion of the present stationary semi-Markovian class in the published causally sufficient setup. The verified binary lag-switch pair remains a direct failure certificate, and all other undecided inputs return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). The revised transition bound is \(5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}\). Every success supports the existing cylinder plug-in and HAC delta-method inference under the stated positivity, mixing, bandwidth, and variance conditions.

project_justification.gap: Published causally sufficient SCG adjustment criteria do cover a substantial cyclic and self-looped subclass, but they do not address latent-confounded summaries or supply a sound-and-complete lag-specific micro-effect decision rule over the present fixed-alphabet stationary refinement class. Fixed-graph hedges likewise do not automatically preserve time homogeneity, exact summary, positivity, equality of the entire process law, and unchanged coordinate alphabets under a refinement switch.
project_justification.niche: The attainable contribution is certified partial identification with graph-native abstention. The procedure imports the published causally sufficient adjustment region, adds saturated-ID successes under latent confounding for acyclic loop-free directed summaries, and gives a direct cyclic lag-switch nonidentification pair for two displayed refinements, each with its own refinement-specific identifying functional. The remaining latent-confounded cyclic cases require the still-open offset-sensitive normal form and direct fixed-alphabet witness construction.
project_justification.fill: The ordered procedure recognizes one proved outside-front-door success, one proved positive stationary lag-switch failure, the explicit Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui adjustment branch whenever its finite SCG predicate holds, and otherwise a memoized ordinary-ID call on at most \(n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\) ancestral roles when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free. It returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) whenever these certified rules do not decide the query. This yields sound finite-cylinder successes for additional cyclic and self-looped causally sufficient summaries while preserving the honest absence of a completeness claim.

body.related_work: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui give sufficient graphical conditions and finite adjustment sets for singleton total effects from directed SCGs under causal sufficiency and consistency throughout time. The present procedure imports that coverage explicitly rather than claiming it as novelty: exact summary and translation invariance provide the SCG relation, time-homogeneous equations provide consistency through time, and the absence of bidirected summary edges together with independent semi-Markovian roots yields causal sufficiency. Assaad's later micro front-door result treats selected latent-confounded effects, Ferreira and Assaad treat macro effects and linear direct effects, and Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier characterize common adjustment under causal sufficiency. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman bound identification after one periodic fine graph is specified; Jaber and coauthors decide the finite graph class represented by one PAG; Shpitser and Pearl prove ID soundness and completeness for one finite ADMG; and Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser define fixed-ADMG reachable graphs and intrinsic sets. These fixed-input results motivate the finite acyclic branch but do not supply the offset-sensitive cross-refinement state invariant or the direct fixed-alphabet rejection construction requested by the open-ended question. The note's new claims therefore remain the stationary transfer, certified combination, and explicit lag-switch obstruction, not the imported adjustment criterion itself.
body.interpretation: A success tag is a positive causal certificate. It may now arise from the concrete outside-front-door rule, the imported causally sufficient SCG adjustment rule, or a successful saturated ordinary-ID call; in every case the returned finite-cylinder arithmetic functional equals the lag-specific intervention probability in every compatible SCM. A failure tag remains a negative certificate consisting of two fixed-alphabet stationary SCMs with the same entire observational process law and different target values. An unknown tag is neither and records that the current sound rules do not decide the query. EasyRCA ranks only successful queries and does not turn either failure or unresolved status into a low transmission score.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The added adjustment branch does not address the core latent-confounded cyclic obstruction because it requires the bidirected summary edge set to be empty. In the unresolved region, a finite rejection witness may contain several temporal roles of the same observed coordinate; independent-shift replication then attempts to place several role values into one coordinate-time variable, while product-slot repairs enlarge the fixed alphabet. The procedure avoids that defect by constructing its only general failure example directly and returning unknown elsewhere. Strict stationarity and bounded structural lag also do not make the observed process finite-order Markov, so transition-kernel truncation and semantic gluing of refinement-specific formulas still cannot supply completeness.
body.honest_scope: The note proves sound partial certification, not a sound-and-complete TID-SCG dichotomy. The Assaad--Devijver--Gaussier--Gössler--Meynaoui branch is imported published coverage under causal sufficiency and only for the paper's stated sufficient graphical condition; no necessity or novelty is claimed for that criterion. The acyclic saturated-ID branch is sound but not claimed complete for uniform identification, the static boundary still returns unknown on ID failure, the front-door result remains the concrete outside-family witness, and the direct failure branch covers the verified binary lag-switch query. Latent-confounded cyclic cases outside these rules remain open. The HAC theorem applies only after a sound success and additionally requires cylinder positivity, geometric beta mixing, the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).
